resources.string: A plugin must not declare its own FileProvider to open or share a file — this tool\'s code runs in the host process, and only the process that owns a provider can grant its content:// Uris. Instead, this sample writes a sample file, mints a host-owned Uri via ShareManager.getShareableUri, and opens it with a custom ACTION_VIEW chooser intent.
Gallery sample — Open With file, opened via a host-owned Uri from ShareManager.getShareableUri.
getShareableUri returned null — the file is outside the host\'s shareable FileProvider roots.

Rule: a plugin-owned FileProvider can never validly grant a Uri to another app, even if its library is bundled — grants can only be issued by the process that owns the provider, and a plugin\'s tool code runs in the host\'s process, not its own. Get a host-owned Uri from ShareManager.getShareableUri instead. Compare with the Host Services sample (Section 12), which shares the same kind of file via the share sheet (ShareManager.shareFile) rather than a custom intent.
